### Bar chart
Ranked or long-labelled categories drawn as horizontal bars from a data table, grouped, stacked or as a meter.

Component ID: `bar-chart`

[Component documentation](https://www.expressivecss.com/bar-chart.html.md) · [Repository source](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/blob/master/docs/src/pages/bar-chart.astro) · [Matching tag](https://github.com/BaezFJ/ExpressiveCSS/tree/v0.20.0)

Contract: ExpressiveCSS 0.20.0

Contract SHA-256: `0de0b2111fe196218a0739efabf3909ed9b89c6b6a14010748f2b219a89c5bcd`

#### Selection and adaptation

Runtime ownership: `auto-init`. No dedicated entry in the reviewed Google component inventory.

Public JavaScript exports: `BarChart`. See the [API index](../references/api-index.md).

Example: Visitors from five traffic sources, longest first, is a bar chart with values inside the bars. Visitors per month for a year is a column chart.

#### Material mapping

Relationship: none. Web extension; no dedicated entry was observed in the reviewed current M3 component inventory.

Support: Horizontal bars drawn from zero from a figure's data table, grouped by row or stacked, with split, track, values and sparkline modifiers, negative values, gaps, a fixed value range, row labels, round value axis labels with .axis, a legend, and a pointer and keyboard tooltip with a highlight band.

Web adaptation: The <table> stays in the page as the text alternative and the no-JavaScript fallback; the bars and their values are aria-hidden and the plot is one Tab stop with a polite live tooltip.

Known boundary: There are no value axis labels.

Full parity remains unassessed. Review provenance and specification links: [capability evidence](../references/capability-roadmap.md#bar-chart).

#### Contract

A `<figure class="bar-chart">` takes the same `<figcaption>` and `<table>` as a column chart. `AutoInit()` draws each row as a band of bars growing from zero along the inline axis, one bar per series, with the row's label at the inline start, a legend when there is more than one series, and a highlight band and tooltip that follow the pointer. The table stays in the page, visually hidden, as the chart's text alternative; without JavaScript it shows instead of the chart.

#### Syntax

```html
<figure class="bar-chart track values">
  <figcaption>Visitors by source</figcaption>
  <table>
    <thead>
      <tr><th>Source</th><th>Visitors</th></tr>
    </thead>
    <tbody>
      <tr><th>Search</th><td data-value="900000">900K</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Social</th><td data-value="650000">650K</td></tr>
      <tr><th>Email</th><td data-value="420000">420K</td></tr>
    </tbody>
  </table>
</figure>
```

#### Also documented

The Bar chart section of the [API reference](https://www.expressivecss.com/llm.md) also covers Tokens.

#### Rules

- `bar-chart-is-a-figure-with-a-table`: Write .bar-chart as a <figure> holding a <table> of the data. The drawn chart is hidden from assistive technology, so the table is all a screen reader reads, and it is what shows without JavaScript.
- `bar-chart-has-a-caption`: Name a .bar-chart with a <figcaption>. It names the focusable plot as well as the figure; hide it with .visually-hidden when nearby text already names the chart.
